stance.label: Short-term bearish, the prior low drew one round of bids but not yet spot money; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: The break of the prior low was bought back on volume; leverage returned first, funding up from 1.3% to 6.3% in a day, and spot money still lags.
summary: Short-term bearish, with selling pressure a little lighter: price broke the low intraday and closed back above $60,000 on volume while Coinbase taker selling narrowed, yet the chasers were perp longs and the ETFs logged a 6th straight outflow. Long-term bullish: total unrealized profit is down to 33.4% of market cap and MVRV Z is the lowest since Jun 30. A close below $58,525 cancels today's bid; ETF inflows and a close above $64,000 would show spot taking over.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 14 straight closes below; the close needs +19.3% to get back above

overview.lead: Yesterday we wrote that $58,525 could only be defended by spot bids; it broke intraday today and the close was pulled back, on 1.56x the prior day's volume and at the very top of the day's range.
points: Close $60,369, intraday low $57,211 and high $60,479 (Kraken); the low came around the US stock open and price recovered from there.

US stocks also sold off first and recovered: the Nasdaq was down about 4.5% early and closed about 0.6% lower, the Dow finished green; core PCE at 3.3% beat forecasts and the new tariffs run up to 20% (Yahoo Finance, CoinDesk).
Fear & Greed 13, the 13th day of extreme fear; November is -22.0% so far, and the worst November since 2013 was 2018's -37.0%.
Nothing new on the exit framework or the market stage; the close has been below the 200-day MA for 14 days.

cycle.lead: Valuation stopped sliding today: the long-term holder loss share sits just under this cycle's high, and the miner-capitulation light came on for the second time in three days.
points: Long-term holder loss share 45.9%, against this cycle's high of 46.5% on Nov 20; a close below roughly $58,000 would take it past that (CheckOnChain, the price level is an estimate).
MVRV Z 0.22, the lowest since 0.18 on Jun 30; NUPL 0.112, also a 147-day low (CoinMetrics, Nov 24).

Hash Ribbons are back in miner capitulation: the 30-day average hashrate is 1,008.4 EH/s, under the 60-day average of 1,013.9 (mempool.space). Hashrate over the last 7 days is still 5.9% above the week before and Friday's difficulty is projected up 9.1%, so the light is on by a hair.
The market stage is still bull, with 7 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA and the rule needing 30 to leave; none of the 6 supporting lights is on.

market.lead: The coins that changed hands over the last 7 days are stacked at $58,000–60,000, and today's low dipped into that stack and bounced; the first hurdle above is the underwater supply at $62,000–64,000.
points: This is where the bids in today's first finding landed: over 7 days the $58,000, $59,000 and $60,000 buckets took in 460K BTC combined while the $64,000 bucket lost 150K BTC (Bitview; on-chain movement is not always a trade).
The down leg is 65 days old and -30.3% on closes; it ends on a close back at $67,627, still 12.0% away.
The close sits at -1.56 standard deviations in the short-term holder cost bands, with -2 at $56,256 (Bitview).

Only 2.7% of the past year's closes are lower than today's; the Sell Pressure Index has been at its maximum for 16 days, a setup seen 20 times since 2012 with a median further drop of 12% before it cleared.

deriv.lead: Leverage turned long again within a day: open interest rose and Hyperliquid flipped from shorts paying back to longs paying; option insurance got a little cheaper, and the money is still buying downside protection.
points: The other half of today's first finding: the weighted funding rate is 6.34% against the 1.30% in yesterday's edition, and market-wide open interest is 327K BTC, up about 5,600 BTC in a day (Coinalyze).
The bounce was no short squeeze: short liquidations for the day were $45.8M and long liquidations $81.6M, both small (Coinalyze, excluding Hyperliquid).

Option defensiveness eased a notch: 25-delta risk reversal -7.1 from -9.2 yesterday; 7-day implied volatility is still 4.9 points above 90-day, and option premium has leaned to puts for 28 days (Deribit).

The estimated long-liquidation band sits at $55.7–57.2K with 11K BTC, and today's low stopped right at its upper edge (several exchanges, an estimate). The order book shows a $193M bid and a $211M offer at $60,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: US spot selling loosened its grip for the first time, with Coinbase trading slightly above offshore venues on the day; the ETF and stablecoin channels are both still draining.
points: The spot side of today's first finding: Coinbase 7-day net taker selling is 5,011 BTC, from 6,674 BTC a day earlier (Coinalyze); the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount was +0.010% on the day after -0.012%.

ETFs lost $235M net on Nov 24, the 6th straight trading day of outflows (CoinMarketCap; Farside has $231M). The 20-trading-day total is now deeper than both 2025 stretches and shallower only than this June's -$5.64B.
Stablecoins $282.5B, down $0.7B in a day and 1.33% over 7 days (DefiLlama); USDT is at $0.9987 with a 7-day average discount of 0.160%, so holders are still converting stablecoins back to dollars.
Rates are tighter still: Polymarket puts a December hike at 95.9%, and the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.61% is 0.61 points above the Fed's upper bound.

onchain.lead: Loss-taking is holding at a high level: long-term holders still realized $4.38B of losses in a week, and across three months of selling, sellers are in the red as a group from today.
points: Today's second finding lives on this page: the network's realized profit ÷ loss summed over 90 days fell to 0.993, having only climbed above 1 on Sep 21 (Bitview).
Long-term holder realized losses over 7 days are $4.38B, from $4.60B a day earlier; the LTH-SOPR 7-day average is 0.742 (Bitview).

Short-term holder loss intensity is 1.91, still under the threshold of 2; STH-SOPR is 0.976, below 1 for 20 days, with 13,161 BTC of losses realized on the day against 2,156 BTC of profit (CheckOnChain).

By address balance, addresses holding 10K+ BTC added 36K BTC over 7 days and the 100–1,000 BTC tier shed 18K BTC (Bitview); the long-term holder 30-day net position is -171K BTC, negative for 113 days (bitcoin-data, Nov 24).

exit.lead: Every exit condition is far off; the nearest needs a rally of more than 80%.
points: 14 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $72,029, 16.2% under it; the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.406, with the 0.75 line at $110,555; the three top indicators read 6 / 5 / 23, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 24).

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost $231.6M net on Nov 24, the sixth straight trading day of outflows; November outflows total $4.94B, past June's $4.51B and the worst month since the funds launched in 2024
news.source: Cointelegraph, 2026-11-25 (SoSoValue data; Bitfinex Alpha cites Farside at $231.4M the same day)
news.read: Our data source shows -$234.5M for Nov 24, so the three sources sit within $3M of each other. The daily outflow was less than half the prior day's $570M and the first under $300M since Nov 17; our 20-trading-day total is -$4.76B, beyond the -$4.71B troughs of the March and November 2025 stretches. Slower outflows are part of the easing in today's first finding, and they need several days in a row to count; the Nov 25 figure is not out yet and Nov 26 is a market holiday.

news.title: US October PCE rose 3.8% year over year (3.6% prior) and core 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast; Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualized and jobless claims were 186K; markets price about a 98% chance of a 25 bp hike in December
news.source: Yahoo Finance, 2026-11-25 (CoinDesk's same-day live coverage has the same figures)
news.read: The last big release before the decision also ran hot, leaving little doubt about a Dec 9 hike. Polymarket on our page puts a hike at 95.9%, with 2.4% on 50 bp or more; the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.91% (FRED, Nov 24). BTC's $57,211 low came after the data, around the US stock open, and it recovered alongside equities. Rates remain a headwind for BTC and the cycle call is unchanged.

news.title: The US proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other trading partners, stacked on existing tariffs and effective January at the earliest; the Nasdaq fell about 4.5% early and closed about 0.6% lower, the Dow ended green and Nvidia closed down about 4%
news.source: Yahoo Finance, 2026-11-25 (intraday figures from CoinDesk the same day)
news.read: The tariffs went from a report to a proposal, at a higher rate than Tuesday's reported cap, with a comment period still ahead. US stocks recovered most of the day's losses and BTC traced the same shape; our 30-day BTC–Nasdaq correlation is 0.76, and BTC has beaten the S&P 500 on only 46.7% of the last 90 US trading days. Part of today's bounce followed equities, and the data cannot separate how much was BTC's own demand. Macro background; the cycle call is unchanged.

news.title: BTC fell to about $57,300 intraday before retaking $60,000; Galaxy withdrew its October call that the bear market ended in June and named the Jun 30 closing low of $58,525 as the key level; Strategy shares touched a multi-year low of $70 intraday and closed near $80
news.read: Our intraday low is $57,211 and the close $60,369 (Kraken), so the daily bar held $58,525. Galaxy's count: when a low that had held for 60+ days after a 20%+ rebound was broken, price fell at least another 17% in all 7 cases; that describes what follows a daily close below, which has not happened. Our records show Strategy holding 851,305 BTC at a 20.0% paper loss; MSCI removes it from its indexes on Nov 30, which pressures the stock and adds no direct BTC selling.

news.title: The US House Financial Services Committee formally reported the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill (H.R. 8957) on Nov 24, making it eligible for a floor vote; Treasury would set up the reserve within 180 days of enactment and hold for at least 20 years, and the committee text dropped the purchase funding from Fed surplus and other sources
news.read: One procedural step forward, with no floor date and no Senate action yet. Without purchase funding the bill mainly locks up coins the government already holds for 20 years, which removes a potential seller and adds no buyer. It brings no immediate money and changes none of our readings.

news.title: Mining pool Braiins reported attackers impersonating pools over unencrypted Stratum V1 connections to hijack hashrate; more than 1,000 mining sites were targeted on Nov 20 and the diverted hashrate grew from 175 PH/s to as much as 1.9 EH/s in two weeks
news.read: 1.9 EH/s is under 0.2% of the network; our 7-day hashrate is 1,040.7 EH/s. Hijacked machines keep mining and only the rewards go to someone else's wallet, so block production is unaffected. For miners it is one more cut to revenue while power costs are already underwater: the close is only 1.5% above our estimated production cost (Bitview). No change to any reading.

news.title: One-year Sharpe ratios for gold and BTC are both negative, at -0.53 and -0.75; gold has dropped 37% from its Jan 28 peak of $5,589 to below $3,500
news.read: Two "havens" are losing money together in a rate-hike regime, so the pressure comes from the dollar and rates and BTC has no problem of its own here. Over the last two months our page shows BTC -28.2% and gold -16.6% (PAXG), with BTC the deeper of the two. It has no bearing on the cycle call and only shows that money is avoiding every non-yielding asset.

findings.title: The break was bought back: spot sellers paused, leverage chased again
findings.lean_why: US spot selling shrinking for the first time is a plus, but perp longs carried price back to $60,000 while ETFs and stablecoins kept draining; one side let go and the other has yet to arrive, so the evidence is mixed.
findings.what: The dip under the prior low found a bid, in the form of spot sellers standing down and leveraged longs chasing: close $60,369 on 1.56x the prior day's volume (Kraken, Nov 25).
findings.why: Start with which side moved. On spot, the sellers stopped: the three spot venues were net taker buyers of 62 BTC on the day after net selling 1,897 BTC the day before; Coinbase 7-day net taker selling narrowed from 6,674 BTC to 5,011 BTC; the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount was +0.010% on the day, the second positive print in 9 days (Coinalyze, Coinbase/Binance). Net taker buying was only 62 BTC, yet price lifted more than $3,000 off the low, so aggressive buying did not push it up; offers were pulled and resting bids absorbed the rest. On derivatives, longs came back: the weighted funding rate is 6.34% against the 1.30% in yesterday's edition, Hyperliquid is back at 10.95%, and market-wide open interest rose about 5,600 BTC in a day to 327K BTC (Coinalyze). It was no short squeeze either, with short liquidations at only $45.8M. What contradicts "a bid showed up" is the source of money: ETFs lost another $235M on Nov 24, stablecoins shrank $0.7B in a day, and OKX spot was a net taker seller of 286 BTC (OKX only). The signal list's "sharp 7-day rise" in the Coinbase premium starts from a figure that does not match the daily series, so only daily values are used here.
findings.alt: The other path is that today was just covering ahead of Thanksgiving: US stocks went from -4.5% to -0.6% the same day, BTC's low and rebound followed their timing, and the bids may not have been aimed at $58,000. Two numbers separate the cases: Coinbase 7-day net taker selling shrinking inside 3,000 BTC means spot pressure is fading; funding rising further while Coinbase selling widens again means leverage is holding price up, and the next drop will have another batch of longs to unwind. Data limits: taker flow counts only aggressive orders and excludes resting fills; Binance's public liquidation feed under-reports and Hyperliquid is absent from the liquidation totals; the Nov 25 ETF figure is not out yet.
findings.history: Longs returning too fast during a decline has been a poor sign before. 72% of Binance accounts are long, in the top 10% since 2021; of the 26 times the share got this high, price was higher 90 days later only 10 times, with a median of -7.0% against +1.9% for any day (Coinalyze).
findings.so: What changed is the premise of yesterday's first finding: we wrote that $60,000 was broken by spot selling and the prior low could only be held by spot bids, and today spot selling eased and the low held once on a daily close. What has not changed is the buyer: new money is still absent and leverage arrived first; the long-term valuation read, in the bottom zone, also stands.
findings.next: By Dec 2: Coinbase spot 7-day net taker selling inside 3,000 BTC would mean pressure is fading and today's bid has spot behind it; a close below $58,525 would mean the bids that showed up today could not hold.

findings.title: Sellers as a group are back in the red, 65 days after leaving
findings.lean_why: Three months of selling add up to a loss, so September's exit from the loss-taking regime did not hold; when it relapsed this fast before, two of those episodes dragged on for more than ten months.
findings.what: The loss-taking regime that ended in September is back: the network's realized profit ÷ realized loss summed over 90 days fell to 0.993, the first reading under 1 since Sep 21 (Bitview, Nov 25).
findings.why: The signal list does not carry this item; the basis is the 90-day view of the realized profit ÷ loss card, which read 1.037 a day earlier. Broken down, the loss side is the one growing: the ratio is 0.145 on a 7-day sum and 0.298 on a 30-day sum, so profits are under a third of losses; network-wide realized losses were $10.5B over 7 days, of which long-term holders took $4.38B. Whose losses: of the last 30 days' realized losses, 50.4% came from coins held under a month and 38.8% from coins bought 1–2 years ago. Other sources point the same way: the aSOPR 7-day average is 0.959, in its lowest 2% of the past year; CoinMetrics' 30-day net realized loss is 1.64% of market cap and broke the cycle-scale line on Nov 23 (Nov 24). The one-year ratio is 0.681 and was already under 1; today the shorter window fell back with it.
findings.alt: The other path is a hairline cross: 0.993 is close to 1, and the 90-day window is rolling off late-August and September profit-taking while November's losses roll in, so a drop in daily losses could lift it back above 1 within days, as in March 2023 when it stayed under for only 5 days. The 30-day ratio separates the cases: back above 0.5 and the 90-day line turns up soon; stuck near 0.3 and the 90-day line keeps falling. Data limits: per-UTXO and not entity-adjusted, so exchange wallet reshuffles inflate both sides; ETF shares change hands off-chain, which may dull this ratio in the ETF era.
findings.history: Falling back within two months of leaving the loss-taking regime opened a long bear market half the time. It has happened 5 times since 2012: after May 2018 and May 2022 the ratio stayed under 1 for more than ten months; March 2012 and March 2020 lasted about three months each; March 2023 lasted only 5 days.
findings.so: What changed is that "September already left the bear-market pattern" no longer holds; this cycle's loss-taking phase is unfinished, the same event as the cycle-scale losses in yesterday's second finding seen through another chart. What has not changed is valuation: unrealized profit is down to 33.4% of market cap, inside past bottom zones, and cheap and still-capitulating can both be true.
findings.next: By Dec 3: the 90-day ratio below 0.95 would mean the loss-taking phase is reopening; back above 1 would mean it was a hairline cross and refute this call.

items.title: Bitcoin's Recovery Remains Elusive
items.points: ETFs lost $231.4M on Nov 24, the first day under $300M since Nov 17, taking November to $4.94B with IBIT at 84%; on Nov 24 open interest rose while price fell 2.4% with funding at 6–8%, read as leveraged longs buying; the base case is $56,300–61,400 into the Nov 27 expiry, and a turn needs three straight ETF inflow days, a hold above $61,300 and STH-SOPR back at 1.
items.meaning: The leveraged long buying it describes shows on our page too: funding at 6.34% and open interest up about 5,600 BTC in a day. None of its three turn conditions is met here: ETFs have six straight outflow days, the close at $60,369 is under $61,300, and STH-SOPR is 0.976. Its range floor of $56,300 was not tested today; the low was $57,211.

items.title: Strategy Watch #10
items.points: The October institutional monthly: BTC's 30-day net inflow peaked at $14.2B on Oct 17 and eased to $9.2B by month end; the 30-day stablecoin flow turned negative on Oct 7 and passed $6B of outflow late in the month; US spot ETFs ended October with a 5.6K BTC outflow, the first since July; average manager cash rose from 12.2% to 15.7%.
items.meaning: It covers October, and November's selling had its early signs there: stablecoins turned negative first and ETFs followed. Our stablecoin supply is now down $17.7B over 30 days and the ETF 20-trading-day total is -$4.76B, both far deeper than its end-October readings.

items.title: The Week On-chain: The Canary in the Coal Mine
items.points: Selling intensified after the $62–66K support broke; realized losses are the heaviest since FTX in November 2022, called the first major capitulation of this bear market; ETF net outflows reached $4.3B over 20 trading days; dealers are short gamma at $58–64K; below a daily close under $60K and the June low of $58.5K, the next level is the realized price at $53.2K.
items.meaning: Its key level of $58.5K broke intraday today and held on the daily close. Our estimated negative gamma is heaviest at $58,000 and the realized price is $53,030 (Bitview); the major capitulation it describes shows up in today's second finding through another chart, with 90-day realized profit below realized loss. Nothing newer on its list.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 48
items.points: Weekly ETF net outflow of $1.7B, the heaviest since early July, with ETF holders' MVRV down to 0.97; futures open interest fell 12% to $29.3B, the lowest since early March; 25-delta skew rose to 17.4%, the highest since mid-July; supply in profit 47.3%, realized cap monthly change -0.93%.
items.meaning: It describes leverage flushed once; our page shows longs returning after the flush, with open interest at 327K BTC and only 1.9% lower over 7 days. Skew began to narrow today, with our 25-delta risk reversal moving from -9.2 to -7.1.

items.title: What Comes Next After a New Cycle Low?
items.points: The Nov 21 low of $55,501 was the lowest since September 2024, after seven straight weekly declines; resistance at $61,300 and the short-term holder cost basis of $72,720, realized price $53,200; base case a $56,800–64,900 range into the Nov 27 expiry, with risk skewed toward a retest of $55,501.
items.meaning: Today's low of $57,211 stayed inside its range and did not retest $55,501; its first resistance at $61,300 has not been reclaimed either. The Nov 25 issue narrows the range to $56,300–61,400.

items.title: The $14 Billion Decision Bitcoin ETF Holders Must Make by December 31
items.points: Paywalled, title only: a decision ETF holders face before year end, sized at $14 billion.
items.meaning: The body was not readable, so no comparison is possible. By our estimate the close is 23.6% below the ETF holders' cost basis and has been under it for 14 days; whether this group sells before year end is what December's ETF flows will show.

items.title: Digital assets digest - November 24th 2026
items.points: The page carries only a headline and a download link: BTC near $60,000 and Fed risk. Its head of research told The Block on Nov 25 that the market is at the tail end of the bear market, with a $60,000–90,000 range and a breakout needing a monetary policy shift.
items.meaning: Its range floor of $60,000 broke intraday today and was reclaimed on the close, by 0.6%. A tail-end bear market matches our long-term read of a bottom zone; today's second finding adds that a tail end can drag on for a long time.

items.title: Institutional Holdings of Bitcoin ETPs Reach New All-Time High
items.points: 13F filers added the equivalent of 49,229 BTC in Q3 and hold a record 356,491 BTC, 27.6% of spot BTC funds; advisers and wealth platforms make up 40.5% of that. Fund holdings fell 38,531 BTC from quarter end to Nov 16.
items.meaning: The wealth-channel clients who came in during Q3 are underwater as a group, and November's record outflow says part of them are redeeming. Separately, on Nov 25 Galaxy withdrew its call that the bear market ended in June and set a daily close below $58,525 as the dividing line, which did not happen today.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC broke below its 200-week MA, ETF exposure is back to mid-August levels and funding is negative; it argues these readings have matched BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: Its funding condition moved further away today: the weighted rate is 6.34% with a 7-day average of 2.09%, as longs returned quickly. Its list shows no newer issue.

cards.dawn: Bullish on the long view: valuation sits in the cycle's coldest zone, with unrealized profit at a 4-year low. But the weekly score flips bearish in 1 more week, and this zone can last months.
cards.avgd: Leaning bullish: price is far below all nine cost lines and averages, a historically cheap zone led by the 200-week MA. Prior bear lows ranked lower, and after 2014's dip it fell 46.6% more.
cards.p20: Bullish: the top is far off. Market heat is under half the prior peak's, with the warning line near $110,555; Pi Cycle and the top gauges are cold too. It says nothing about the bottom.
cards.lthloss: Leaning bullish: the share of long-term holders underwater is in past bear-bottom range, but still hugging the 11/20 high. A close below about $58,000 sets a new high and breaks the pattern.
cards.cyccmp: Neutral: this cycle has fallen far less from its top than prior ones, which were down 76–83% by now. The bottom may be higher, or not in yet; a break of the June low pushes it later.
cards.levels: Bearish: price sits below most cost lines, so active investors and ETF buyers are underwater. First overhead is the 200-day MA near $72K; reclaiming the $76,044 true market mean restores the bulls.
cards.urpd: Neutral: a thick pile of coins sits just above at 62K–64K, where buyers break even and tend to sell. Coins moving this month mostly moved at a loss, as high buyers hand supply down lower.
cards.strike: Neutral: December's big expiry has the most puts at $60,000, right where price sits, while calls stack far off at $80,000. Negative gamma below can amplify drops; pull toward max pain is weakly evidenced.
cards.legs: Bearish: the down leg is already deeper than 92% of the last 12 declines, yet not over. Only a close back at $67,627 turns it into an up leg; bounces before that stay inside this leg.
cards.pullback: Bearish: pullback pressure is still maxed, with three conditions met for nearly a month. Past cases saw a −1.4% median 90 days on, common mid-bear; it eases once two of the three clear.
cards.profit: Leaning bullish, contrarian: almost every recent buyer is underwater. Past moves above 60% saw a +8.4% median a month later, but in bear markets the share can sit above 90% for long stretches.
cards.sopr: Bearish: recent buyers have sold at a loss for 20 days, deeper than the late-October dip. The handover of these coins is done only when sellers as a whole get back to breaking even.
cards.rpl: Bearish for now: a year of losses outweighing profits puts this in past bottom territory, but 7-day losses still run 7x profits and the ratio hasn't turned. A rebound to 0.75 confirms the low.
cards.miners: Bearish: miners are losing money on power, with price below the $66,222 break-even for mainstream rigs, yet difficulty is set to rise 9.1%. Price is only 1.5% above estimated production cost.
cards.etf: Bearish: institutions keep stepping back. ETFs saw 6 straight days of outflows, about 9.7x what miners mined over the span, and price is 20% under Strategy's average cost.
cards.pr-us: Neutral: US and offshore demand look about even; most of the Coinbase discount is USDT trading under $1. Still, stablecoins are being swapped back to dollars and Coinbase spot sells heavier than usual.
cards.ad: Bearish: new demand isn't absorbing supply. Both 30-day and 1-year apparent demand are negative, new capital stopped flowing in 12 days ago, and stablecoins shrank $17.7B in a month.
cards.whale: Bearish: whales cut holdings this month, led by the 100–1K BTC tier, and kept selling last week. Long-term holders are net sellers too; whales ease off only when the 30-day total turns up.
cards.svd: Bearish: sellers still take the initiative in spot. OKX shows more market sells over 7 days and big orders sold over 30. Coinbase selling is easing, but buyers must lead on 7 days to count.
cards.stk: Bearish: BTC is the weakest asset of the past two months, down more than Nasdaq and gold while tracking Nasdaq closely. Markets price a 96% chance of a hike, so the backdrop isn't helping.
cards.fh: Neutral: leverage isn't crowded but is coming back. Funding stays low on a weekly basis yet jumped several-fold in a day, and 72% of Binance accounts are long. Above 30% usually brings a flush.
cards.vol: Neutral: options price bigger moves than recently seen, with implied vol near a 1-year high and front months 4.9 points over 90-day. Volatility says how far, not which way.
cards.oi: Leaning bearish: the biggest open-interest block expires 12/25, premium has favored puts for 28 days and puts trade richer than calls. Evidence that price gets pulled up to max pain is thin.
cards.fng: Bearish short term: sentiment sits in extreme fear, up from neutral a month ago. Past first drops into it saw a −6.1% median 30 days on, often not the low; back above 25 means panic is fading.
